instructions: Put the glass noodles in a large bowl and cover them with hot tap water. Leave them for 10 minutes, until they're soft but still a little firm. Drain them well and snip them a few times with scissors.

Meanwhile, cut the bacon into 1/2 inch pieces. Smash the garlic. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro stems and keep the leaves for the end. Cut the ginger into thin strips, slice the celery and the scallions, and pat the shrimp dry.
In a bowl, whisk 3/4 cup water, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 3 tbsp tamari, 2 tbsp sesame oil, 1 1/2 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp pepper.
Put a wide pot with a lid over medium heat. Add the bacon and cook for 4 minutes, until the fat melts and the edges start to brown.
Add the garlic and the cilantro stems and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the noodles and pour the sauce over them. Toss with tongs until they're coated.
Scatter the ginger over the noodles. Lay the shrimp on top in a single layer, then add the celery and scallions.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and curled and the noodles have taken up most of the sauce.
Take the pot off the heat and toss everything together. Serve in bowls with the cilantro leaves on top.
method_notes: The lead (Hungry in Thailand, 5.0 from 2) has too few ratings, so this is a fallback lead. It layers soaked glass noodles, a sauce, ginger and prawns in a covered pot over bacon and garlic, and steams them for about 5 minutes. Kikkoman's version agrees on the layering but uses evaporated milk and a dipping sauce, which are left out. Wheat is removed: tamari takes the place of the dark soy and Golden Mountain sauce, cilantro stems replace coriander roots and celery replaces Chinese celery. Check the oyster sauce label for wheat.
